subtopic: OIL-GOVERNMENT INTENTIONS WITH REGARD TO PRICE INCREASE
OIL-GOVERNMENT INTENTIONS WITH REGARD TO PRICE INCREASE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, my question is for the Prime Minister. Last Friday I asked him a question regarding the statement by the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources that the government had made a basic decision with regard to the

price of crude oil which he expected would go into effect on July 1. The Prime Minister replied that he was consulting with the Premiers, but press reports since that time indicate that Premier Davis said an increase at this time would not be appropriate, that Premier Lougheed said no decision had been reached and that Premier Schreyer stated the Prime Minister told him no decision was made concerning either the amount or the time of the increase. In light of these statements, I wish to ask the Prime Minister if he can assure the House that it is not the intention of the government to raise the price of crude oil in Canada in the month of July?

speakeroldname: Right Hon. P. E. Trudeau (Prime Minister):
subtopic: OIL-GOVERNMENT INTENTIONS WITH REGARD TO PRICE INCREASE
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I would have to repeat my answer of the other day which the hon. member has summed up pretty well. Obviously, the cabinet and the Minister of Energy, Mines and Resources have explored various possibilities and I am now in the process of examining them with the provinces. It was our hope that we would reach a consensus. I agree with the hon. gentleman that that hope is dimming. I have still not been able to reach all premiers but some will be talking to me later today. Until I have spoken to them all, I would say there is no firm decision yet either in respect of price or timing.

subtopic: OIL-GOVERNMENT INTENTIONS WITH REGARD TO PRICE INCREASE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, may I ask the Prime Minister if it is the intention of the government to proceed with the course of action he forecast in his speech to the first ministers at the conference on April 9 when he said:
But the price for the year beginning in July will have to be higher than it is now.
May I ask the Prime Minister if that is the framework within which the government intends to operate or is there some reason the government intends to follow a different course of action?

subtopic: OIL-GOVERNMENT INTENTIONS WITH REGARD TO PRICE INCREASE
speechtext: Yes, Mr. Speaker; the position of the federal government is the same, that the price of Canadian oil which is substantially below world prices will have to increase if indeed we do not want to run out of this very important commodity. But as to what the price should be or the timing, I repeat that I cannot announce this until I have spoken to all the premiers.

subsubtopic: JUSTIFICATION OF DETENTION ORDER AGAINST "HMS HERMES"-GOVERNMENT POSITION
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, my question is for the Attorney General, but in his temporary absence from the House I will put it to the Acting Secretary of State for External Affairs. Can the minister advise the House whether he feels that the federal court judge was justified in issuing an order to try to detain a warship of a friendly country in support of a civil action against two members of the crew, an action which has not been tried by the court? Does he agree that this should not be done?

speakeroldname: Hon. Mitchell Sharp (Acting Secretary of State for External Affairs):
speakerposition: President of the Privy Council; Leader of the Government in the House of Commons; Liberal Party House Leader
subsubtopic: JUSTIFICATION OF DETENTION ORDER AGAINST "HMS HERMES"-GOVERNMENT POSITION
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, officers of my former department have been in touch with the Department of Justice and the Judge Advocate General's office with a view to clarifying the factual situation. On the basis of the facts as we know them, HMS Hermes is a warship in the service of a foreign state. Hence, under international law and as recognized both in common law and in various Canadian statutes, such a warship would enjoy immunity. It would appear that any court order issued against it would have no legal basis.

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I have a question for the Prime Minister. Statistics Canada issued over the weekend figures-which I am sure the Prime Minister has studied in detail and with which he is fully familiar-which show clearly that the performance of the gross national product in the first quarter was the worst performance in 14 years in any quarter. In view of the fact that if we continue to perform at this rate for the remainder of the year, we will be 6 per cent below last year in GNP, the worst year in 21, does the government now at long last intend to introduce measures to get at the root causes of this economic malaise which has been besetting the country for the past year and a half?

speakeroldname: Right Hon. P. E. Trudeau (Prime Minister):
subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, if the hon. member had studied the figures as diligently as he rightly assumes that I have, he would know that the root causes are practically entirely due to the fact that our foreign trade has fallen off. He would also know that the countries to which we usually do a great deal of selling are now unable to purchase. The root cause, therefore, is something in our outside markets, not in Canada.

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: As I feel sure that the Prime Minister is aware that a great deal of the malaise is due to causes within the country and that these causes can be cured by measures which have been outlined to the government by members of the opposition on a number of occasions in this House, is he going to pay some attention to those suggestions and do something at long last, or will we have to continue with the band-aid measures which have allowed the economy to slide so badly for the last year and a half?

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, that was somewhat a repetition of the first question.

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Hear, hear!

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Hear, hear!

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: You simply must get better writers, Pierre. That isn't sharp enough.

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: After having pointed out in my first answer that the deterioration is almost entirely due to the deterioration in foreign trade balance, I want to say that in so far as domestic demand is concerned, final domestic demand in real terms in Canada resumed its growth following the decline in the fourth quarter. It has resumed its growth in the first quarter, and that should indicate to the hon. member that the government is on the right track.

subsubtopic: DECLINE IN GROSS NATIONAL PRODUCT-GOVERNMENT MEASURES TO COUNTERACT
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I have a final supplementary. If it is all the fault of our customers outside the country, would the Prime Minister explain why imports into this country last year from foreign countries increased by 13 per cent while our exports decreased by 4 per cent? REASON FOR FAILURE TO ACHIEVE OBJECTIVE OF DELIVERY WITHIN ONE DAY
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, a question for the Postmaster General. Is it the intention of the Post Office to ensure that all first class mail posted in major centres in Canada reach its destination within one day? If so, why has the success rate of this program been minimal and what changes are planned in the Post Office delivery system to ensure that its objective of one day delivery is met?

maintopic: REASON FOR FAILURE TO ACHIEVE OBJECTIVE OF DELIVERY WITHIN ONE DAY
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, the hon. gentleman will be very pleased to know that the degree of efficiency and productivity of the Post Office has dramatically improved over the last ten days, particularly in the general Montreal area. We do not pretend to deliver mail the same day. There are certain factors such as the time of day that the letter is mailed, the time of pick up and other things that affect the mail. Having been the strongest critic of the service over the last month, perhaps the House will permit me to congratulate the postal workers on the tremendous increase in efficiency in the last few weeks.

maintopic: DELAY OF MAIL ADDRESSED TO LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION

speakeroldname: Hon. Robert L. Stanfield (Leader of the Opposition):
maintopic: DELAY OF MAIL ADDRESSED TO LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I have a supplementary question for the Postmaster General who has just referred to the efficiency of the department. I wonder if my own experience is part of this. I received a special delivery envelope from the Post Office in Halifax on Saturday night, June 14. It contained letters addressed to my home in Ottawa, to myself and my wife, many of which had been mailed in Ottawa about May 27 or May 28. Included was an invitation to the unveiling of the mural in the Lester B. Pearson Building. I should like to ask the minister whether this is an example of the increased efficiency of the Post Office?

maintopic: DELAY OF MAIL ADDRESSED TO LEADER OF THE OPPOSITION
speechtext: No, Mr. Speaker. I sincerely regret that such an incident should have occurred. I am embarrassed by the fact that the invitation should have been delayed. I can only say that we deliver five billion pieces of mail per year and we need only be inefficient 1 per cent of the time to have 50 million potential problems. subtopic: ALLEGED DELAY OF MAIL WHEN POSTAL CODE USED- REASON FOR PERMITTING MAIL TO BEAR STAMP TELLING PUBLIC TO IGNORE CODE

speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, this is honestly a very difficult question to answer. By some strange coincidence whenever there has been in the past a concerted effort to convince the public not to use the code, more of our mail arrives with the code. We will not be fully automated until 1980, but since 80 per cent of the mail is used by 20 per cent of the public,

namely private industry, and since their acceptance of the code is understandable and they have certain time limits to conform to, we have no concern at all but that the code will be well accepted by the time there is a greater degree of automation across Canada.

subtopic: ALLEGED DELAY OF MAIL WHEN POSTAL CODE USED- REASON FOR PERMITTING MAIL TO BEAR STAMP TELLING PUBLIC TO IGNORE CODE
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, why is it that mail passing through the Canadian Post Office bears the stamp saying "Ignore the Postal Code." Apparently it is put on at the request of the Canadian Labour Congress. subtopic: ALLEGED DELAY OF MAIL WHEN POSTAL CODE USED- REASON FOR PERMITTING MAIL TO BEAR STAMP TELLING PUBLIC TO IGNORE CODE
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, the postal code represents a degree of insecurity to many workers, as automation in the past has led to a reduction of the work force. We have done our best to convince postal workers that this is not the case in the post office. As we are a country with a democratic heritage, we prefer to convince people to use the postal code instead of making the use of the code mandatory by law; but if that were necessary, we would not hesitate to do so.

subtopic: ALLEGED DELAY OF MAIL WHEN POSTAL CODE USED- REASON FOR PERMITTING MAIL TO BEAR STAMP TELLING PUBLIC TO IGNORE CODE
speechtext: A supplementary question, Mr. Speaker. Is the stamp being used by the post office authorities or postal employees, in enjoining people of Canada not to use the code? I ask this because of the strong objections when the town of Tisdale endeavoured to use the stamp "The Land of Rape and Honey" on its mail a few years ago, and the Post Office Department refused to grant permission for use of the stamp. Why is the stamp calling on the Canadian people not to use the postal code being affixed on mail right in the post office?

subtopic: ALLEGED DELAY OF MAIL WHEN POSTAL CODE USED- REASON FOR PERMITTING MAIL TO BEAR STAMP TELLING PUBLIC TO IGNORE CODE
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, as I recall, the Post Office Department thought the word "honey" was too sweet. The word "rape" did not upset them. I assure the right hon. gentleman that the post office authorities are not imprinting the slogan "Boycott the Code" on the mail. This is being done by employees or members of trade unions who are in sympathy with a small number of postal workers, and they have no right to impose this slogan on the envelope.
May I say to the right hon. gentleman who is a well known friend of labour that the present climate between the Post Office and the union is better than it has been for many months. I should like this to continue in the present vein indefinitely, certainly until we obtain a collective agreement with the Canadian Union of Postal Workers, with whom negotiations will begin this coming Thursday.
